title: fix(mcp)!: the objectstack://objects resources read the stdio transport's merged object view, so a package's objects are listed and described
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu4BM6tVgxhg4qFQsbuRHiy9)_

Fixes #25245

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

The stdio MCP transport's two object resources, `objectstack://objects` and `objectstack://objects/{objectName}`, now read the same objects its `list_objects` and `describe_object` tools answer from since #25243: the protocol's merged listing, the one `GET /api/v1/meta/object` serves. They read the `metadata` service until now, so on a kernel with an `environmentId` they listed none of a package's boot-registered objects and answered `404` for each, while the tools listed and described them. The merged read is shared, not copied: `stdio-data-bridge.ts` exports one view, the tools answer from it, and `plugin.ts` gives the same view to its runtime, whose two object resources read it. No published signature moves.

## The defect, measured on base `0b8bce40e0`

`bridgeResources` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`) built `objectstack://objects` from `metadataService.listObjects()` and `objectstack://objects/NAME` from `metadataService.getObject(NAME)`. That service holds a copy of an object only where something put one there. On a kernel with an `environmentId` (`createStandaloneStack`: `os dev` as `env_local`, `os serve`, `os start`; and the cloud single-environment runtime) nothing copies an object a package registers in the `SchemaRegistry` during the boot.

Real kernels (`ObjectKernel` + `MetadataPlugin` + `ObjectQLPlugin`), driven through the real `MCPServerPlugin` stdio session over an in-process transport speaking a stdio client's JSON-RPC, with the fixture package #25243's pins use (two objects, one declared `apiEnabled: false`):

| shape, when the package registered | `resources/read objectstack://objects` | `resources/read objectstack://objects/qa_pkg_open` | `list_objects` / `describe_object` on the same kernel |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `env_local`, during the boot | **`{ objects: [], totalCount: 0 }`** | **`{ error: 'Object "qa_pkg_open" not found', code: 'RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND', status: 404 }`** | both listed, both described |
| `env_local`, installed after the boot (`source: 'marketplace'`) | both listed | described | both listed, both described |
| no `environmentId`, during the boot | both listed | described | both listed, both described |
| no `environmentId`, installed after the boot | both listed | described | both listed, both described |

**A disabled package (`registry.disablePackage`).** On the shape without an `environmentId` the boot copied both objects into the `metadata` service, and the copy outlives the disable: both resources still listed and described them, while `list_objects` and `describe_object` omit them since #25243 and `GET /api/v1/meta/object` omits them. On `env_local` there is no copy, so the resources already omitted them.

## What changed

- **`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`.** New `stdioObjectView(reads)` returns `{ listObjects, getObject }`: the protocol's merged listing (`readMergedObjects`, unchanged from #25243), and a name looked up in that same listing, so a name the listing omits is absent on both reads. A host with no merged read gets the `metadata` service's `listObjects()` / `getObject()`, as before. The bridge's `listObjects` and `describeObject` now answer through this view; their answers do not change (the #25243 unit pins pass unchanged). Exported within the package only; `index.ts` does not publish it.
- **`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`.** New type `McpObjectView`: the `listObjects` and `getObject` members of `IMetadataService`, picked. `buildObjectListResource` and `buildObjectSchemaResource` take it as an optional last parameter and read their objects from it; it defaults to the `metadata` service, so every existing caller reads exactly as before. New package-internal `setRuntimeObjectView(runtime, view)` records a runtime's view in a module-level `WeakMap`; the two object resources registered by `bridgeResources` look it up at each `resources/read` and fall back to the `metadata` service. `bridgeResources` keeps its published signature: a third parameter would have made a new type reachable from the exported `MCPServerRuntime`, a public-surface widening for wiring between this package's own plugin and runtime. The completeness verdict is still asked of the `metadata` service (`diagnoseListRead` on the listing, `diagnoseEmptyRead` on a miss), as the `list_objects` tool asks it.
- **`packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts`.** The `protocol` accessor #25243 added (resolved at each use, `undefined` when absent or throwing, never captured in `start()`) moves out of the stdio branch, because the resources are bridged whether or not this process starts the stdio transport. Before `bridgeResources`, the plugin calls `setRuntimeObjectView(this.runtime, stdioObjectView({ metadataService, protocol }))`. The data bridge and the record resource's gate keep reading the same accessor.
- **`packages/mcp/README.md`.** One paragraph under Resources saying what the two object resources read.
- **`.changeset/25245-mcp-stdio-object-resources-merged.md`.** A `patch` for `@objectstack/mcp`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; both declaration lines are in the body.

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes, old to new, on the stdio transport:

1. **`resources/read objectstack://objects` on a kernel with an `environmentId`, for an object a package or plugin registered during the boot.** Old: omitted, `totalCount` short. New: listed; the non-`sys_` set is what `list_objects` lists.
2. **`resources/read objectstack://objects/NAME` on such an object.** Old: `{ error: 'Object "NAME" not found', code: 'RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND', status: 404 }`. New: the schema body, equal to what `describe_object` answers for NAME.
3. **Both resources on a disabled package's objects, where the `metadata` service still holds a copy** (the narrowing). Old: listed, and described from the copy. New: omitted, and `objectstack://objects/NAME` answers the `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` body, as `describe_object` answers "not found".
4. **An object whose served definition differs from the `metadata` service's copy.** Old: the resources described the copy. New: they describe the definition REST serves.
5. **Both resources while the protocol's merged listing throws.** Old: the `metadata` service's answer. New: the protocol's error travels to the client as a JSON-RPC error, as `list_objects` lets it travel since #25243; nothing falls back. Pinned with a throwing double, not on a real store outage.

Unchanged: objects that already had a copy (every object on a kernel without an `environmentId`, a marketplace install on any kernel, a runtime-authored object) are listed and described as before. A loader outage still withholds `totalCount` (`partial: true`, `returnedCount`, `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`), and a miss during an outage still answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. A host with no `protocol` service, or one without the merged listing, reads the `metadata` service, byte-identically (pinned). A host that builds its own `MCPServerRuntime` and calls `bridgeResources` reads the `metadata` service, as before. The published surface does not move: the built `dist/index.d.ts` declares `bridgeResources` with the same two parameters, and names none of `McpObjectView`, `setRuntimeObjectView` and `stdioObjectView` as declarations. The record resource is untouched. Discovery stays ungated: the resource lists and describes an object declared `apiEnabled: false`, as `list_objects` and `describe_object` do.

## Pins

- **`packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-package-object-discovery.test.ts`, 10 new cases on real kernels, beside #25243's tool pins (80 cases in the file).** For each of the four rows above: `objectstack://objects` lists both package objects, has no `partial`, has `totalCount` equal to its length, and lists the same non-`sys_` names `list_objects` lists; `objectstack://objects/NAME` answers both objects, `enableFeatures.apiEnabled: false` included, each body EQUAL to `describe_object`'s, and a name nothing serves answers exactly `{ error: 'Object "qa_pkg_nowhere" not found', code: 'RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND', status: 404 }`. For a disabled package on both shapes: neither object is listed, and each answers that `404` body.
- **`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.merged-object-resources.test.ts`, 14 cases, doubles.** The listing from the merged read where the copy is absent, the `metadata` service's `listObjects` never asked; a disabled package's objects omitted from both resources although the copy holds them; the `partial` verdict kept from `listDiagnosed`; the `503` on a miss kept from `getDiagnosed`; a throwing merged read propagated by both builders, the copy never asked; the schema body equal to `describeObject`'s for both package objects; no protocol, and a protocol without `getMetaItems`, byte-identical to the `metadata` service alone; a protocol registered after the bridge read on the next call. Over a real `resources/read` on an `MCPServerRuntime`: both resources answer from the view `setRuntimeObjectView` gave, never the `metadata` service; a view given after `bridgeResources` is read on the next call; a runtime given no view reads the `metadata` service, and another runtime's view is not its own.

**Red before, green after.** Each leg's direction was predicted before it ran. The dogfood file consumes `@objectstack/mcp`'s `dist/`, so every leg rebuilt it, and `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` proved the leg's marker reached `dist/` (exit 0) and, after the restore and a rebuild at HEAD, that none remained (`--absent`, exit 0 for each). Mutations were landed and restored by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed; restored blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty).

| leg | mutation | dogfood (80) | unit (14) |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| main | the base tree `0b8bce40e0` (source blobs `6ca41ee187`, `f6d8800263`, `e71d1f1c81`) with the new dogfood pins | 3 failed, 77 passed: the `env_local` during-boot listing and schema; the no-`environmentId` disabled package's resources | not run (the file imports names absent on base) |
| bridge | the runtime's two resources ignore the view their host gave (`runtimeObjectViews.get(this)` replaced) | the same 3 failed | 2 failed: both resources answer from the view; a view given after `bridgeResources` is read |
| plugin | `plugin.ts` gives its runtime no view | the same 3 failed | 14 passed (this file drives the runtime, not the plugin) |
| viewcopy | the view's `getObject` falls back to the copy for a name the listing omits | 2 failed: the no-`environmentId` disabled package's resources, and its `describe_object` (#25243's row, which reads the same view) | 1 failed: a name the listing omits is the coded miss |
| fix | `a697b07f34` | 80 passed | 14 passed |

The legs and the fix row were measured on `a697b07f34`. The final head differs from it by one doc comment in `mcp-server-runtime.ts` (a `{@link}` to the package-internal setter, which the published declaration file would have carried as a dangling link, now plain code text); both pin files are re-run on the final head by the unit suite and the battery below. An earlier local revision passed the view as a third parameter of `bridgeResources`; it was replaced before the first push for the public-surface reason above, and its legs read the same way.

## Local verification

On `5cf1aa4ce3`, the final commit, over `origin/main` `0b8bce40e0` (it has since moved two commits, #25258 and #25259, neither touching `packages/mcp`, `packages/metadata-protocol` or this dogfood file), or on `dc7bee12dc` where a line says so; the one commit between them (`5cf1aa4ce3`) changes how the dogfood pin file's resource helper is typed, not what any case asserts. Every heavy run went through the verify lock, and each line cites its `VERDICT`.

- `@objectstack/mcp` unit suite (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp test`), on `dc7bee12dc`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`; Test Files 42 passed (42), Tests 532 passed (532).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp typecheck`, on `dc7bee12dc`: `VERDICT command-exit 0` (`tsc --noEmit`, and `check:test-typecheck` OK: 6 files, 53 errors, 8 pinned signatures held in the ledger).
- `turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs`, on `dc7bee12dc`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 76 of 76 tasks.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck` with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The first run, on `dc7bee12dc`, answered exit 2 with one error (TS2339): the pin's record reader called `this.readResource` inside the returned object literal, whose `this` tsc types as `Booted` or a `PromiseLike` of it. `5cf1aa4ce3` reads both through a local helper.
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`), on `dc7bee12dc`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`; `eslint --no-inline-config` on the one file `5cf1aa4ce3` changes: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 70 families derived; each run, every one `exit 0` (the second pass, on the final head; the first pass, on `dc7bee12dc`, also answered 70 of 70 `exit 0`).
- `--ran` reconciliation: `70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --event PAYLOAD`, with PAYLOAD a `pull_request` event carrying this title and body: exit 0 (`✓ LEVEL AXIS`: `no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a non-protocol change at `patch`).
- `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --body` on this body: exit 2, its "closing declarations found" answer: `Fixes #25245` and nothing else, bound by the duplicate-fix guard's and the part-of guard's parsers.
- The full dogfood battery, once (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, no shard), on `dc7bee12dc`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`; Test Files 289 passed, 3 skipped (292); Tests 2491 passed, 18 skipped (2509); no failure. It was not re-run for `5cf1aa4ce3`, which touches that one pin file's helper; the file was re-run on the final head: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 80 of 80.

## Acceptance notes

- **Same family, left as it was: the prompt bridge captures the protocol once.** `bridgePrompts` reads skills through `mergedRead`, which `plugin.ts` resolves once in `start()` (#8328), not at each use as the object reads now are. Not this card's defect (skills, not objects), and not measured here.
- **`objectstack://objects/NAME` reads the whole merged listing per call**, as `describe_object` does since #25243 and the HTTP bridge since #25136.
- **File surface.** Beside `mcp-server-runtime.ts` and `plugin.ts`, the fix exports the shared view from `stdio-data-bridge.ts` (the card's "not a second copy of the merge"), adds one README paragraph, and adds the real-kernel pins to the file #25243's tool pins live in. Claim revision 6346855817 names this surface and the `(narrowing)` arm, which the first claim (6346581465) wrote as a bare `no` before the disabled-package reading was measured.
- **Branch name.** This PR's branch is `claude/project-thread-dkk3hd`, the name the session was given, not `claude/issue-25245-…`; the Duplicate Fix Guard may say so.
